**Date:** [January 1887][^1]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Romanes, [<i>Appreciation</i>](other_books/otherbook_241.qmd),  180.
:::

[To [Elizabeth Barnett](people/person_113.qmd)]

I have been reading [an article](other_books/otherbook_1101.qmd) in the *[National Review](organizations/other_259.qmd)*, showing how utterly [Carlyle](people/person_1972.qmd) misquoted Cromwell’s speeches, and absolutely neglected shoals of contemporary papers which would have spoilt his conceptions of his idol. It is curious, but really, poor old Carlyle must have been a good deal of a humbug for all his bluster.

---

[^1]: The article referred to was no doubt Reginald F. D. Palgrave, 'Carlyle, the \\"pious editor\\" of Cromwell's speeches'   *National Review*  8 (January 1887), 588-604.
